name: cpp-cmake
title: CMake (C++14, AUTOSAR profile)
summary: `dsdlc_generate(LANGUAGE cpp ... VOCABULARY vocabulary.yaml)` generates the `autosar` profile with its span bound to CETL's. The vocabulary file is an input of the generation like the definitions are, so editing a binding regenerates.
notes:
The `autosar` profile is C++14, which has no `std::span`, and dsdlc carries no binding for it: without a `--vocabulary` file the run fails naming the concept and the flag. `vocabulary.yaml` binds CETL's `cetl::pf20::span`, and the build fetches CETL at the tag the file was written against.

dsdlc lists a vocabulary file among the run's inputs, which is how `dsdlc_generate()` -- and the Makefile recipe's depfiles, and `rules_dsdl` -- come to depend on it without being told twice. Change the binding and the types regenerate; delete the file and configure fails.

The round-trip program reads a wire-flat type through its accessors as well as serialising the `SystemHealth` the other rows use, so the span the vocabulary binds appears in the program's own source.

requires.reason: compiles the generated C++ and the round-trip program
